description: Pilot Study of Reservoir Sustainability Options: Bighorn Reservoir is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. As extended droughts and severe flooding become more common, they impact water levels and combined with large amounts of sediment, further impact the amount of water available to stakeholders. Coverage: Bighorn Reservoir (2021). The toolkit gives Bighorn Reservoir as the location, 2021 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: As extended droughts and severe flooding become more common, they impact water levels and combined with large amounts of sediment, further impact the amount of water available to stakeholders. Using a sediment wall as a management tool for sediment accumulation will provide insight on sediment accumulation management for all reservoirs, and better address reservoir sedimentation and other stakeholders’ needs.
